title: Queen Vaidehi
hookLine: imprisoned by her son Ajatasattu, the queen asks for a land without sorrow (Amitayur-dhyana, Takakusu)

cards: A prison inside a palace. King Bimbisara, a follower of the Buddha, has been locked away by his own son, Prince Ajatasattu, who means to let him starve. Nobody may bring him food.
But every day the queen visits. First she bathes, covers her body with a paste of honey and flour, and hides juice inside her jewelry. Behind the locked door, in secret, the king eats.
Day after day, he lives. Her story opens a sutra, and her name is today's word: Queen Vaidehi.

teach.h: THE SWORD, AND THE LOCKED ROOM.
teach.b: First, the discovery. The prince learns his father is still alive, and why. He draws his sword against his own mother.
His ministers stop him, warning that killing her would be a crime beyond anything a king should do. So he doesn't kill her; he locks her away too. Second, the cry.
Alone and grieving, Vaidehi turns toward Vulture Peak, where the Buddha is staying, bows, and asks for help. The Buddha comes. She throws herself down in tears: what did I do to have a son like this?
Then she asks for something larger than rescue. Show me a land without sorrow and trouble, where I can be born. I don't want this world anymore.

teach.h: LANDS SHOWN IN A RAY OF LIGHT.
teach.b: The sutra says light streams from between the Buddha's brows, and in it appear the lands of the Buddhas, one after another. She looks at them all, and chooses the land of Amitabha.
Then she asks the question the rest of the sutra answers: how do I see it?
Fourth, who receives this teaching. Not a monk on a mountain, not a scholar in a hall. A mother and a wife, locked in a room after the worst day of her life.
Some Pure Land teachers read Vaidehi as an ordinary person, the kind the teaching was always meant for. The meditations that follow are given to grief, because grief asked.

how: The sutra that opens with Vaidehi's story, the Amitayur-dhyana or meditation sutra, is chanted and studied in Chinese and Japanese Pure Land communities alongside the two sutras on the land of bliss.

o: the Buddha's mother, who died soon after his birth
the queen who founded the first Pure Land temple in India
a grieving queen who asked for a land without sorrow

p: smuggled food in honey and flour

s: Vaidehi asked the Buddha to punish her son
she asked for a land without sorrow, and how to see it.
she fed the starving king with a paste of honey and flour on her body
and hid juice inside her jewelry.
she chose Amitabha's land after seeing the lands of the Buddhas
they appeared in light from between the Buddha's brows.

games.q: you're Vaidehi: locked away, your husband starving, your son holding a sword. the Buddha comes to you. what do you ask?
o: for your son to be punished.
for a land without sorrow, and how to see it.
for nothing; you send him away.
games.why: she asks for more than rescue: a land without sorrow. her question, how do I see it, opens the meditations of the sutra.

practice: Bring to mind one person carrying sorrow right now, a friend, a parent, someone in the news, maybe yourself, and see their face clearly.
Breathe in and notice their sorrow without fixing it; breathe out and silently wish them free of it, in plain words of your own, one breath at a time, the way metta practice does.
And if the sorrow is yours and you don't want to be alive, please call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Queen Vaidehi. The imprisoned queen of the meditation sutra, who asked the Buddha for a land without sorrow and chose the land of Amitabha. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Vaidehi, a name meaning 'the woman of Videha'. in Japanese she is Idaike (韋提希).

carryVoice: Your line: a land without sorrow. Her next question was how to see it. That's the week, done.
